international.title: ‘No time for a culture war’: Victoria’s electricity supply is at risk. Can it avoid power shortages and bill shocks?
international.summary: State faces electricity supply gap when Yallourn coal-fired power station closes in 2028 as experts warn neither Labor nor the Coalition has adequate plans Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here Victoria’s electricity supply will be at risk when a major power plant shuts in 2028 and neither major party is offering a plan at this month’s state election to deal with it, experts have warned. All parties concede the giant Yallourn coal plant, which has operated in the Latrobe Valley since the 1970s and supplies a fifth of Victoria’s energy, is at the end of its functional life and will shut in less than two years. Analysts say the parties vying to run the state are failing to properly explain how they will fill the power shortfall the closure will create.
